summary: Houthi militants attacked two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea, pushing Brent crude above $100 a barrel for the first time in two months, driving inflation fears that hammered equities and pressured bonds. Separately, the U.S. trade representative unveiled a new wave of tariffs on 60 trading partners to replace the temporary 10% global surcharge that expired today, with rates of 10% to 12.5% now locked in.
tweet: Brent topping $100 on Houthi Red Sea attacks and a fresh wave of U.S. tariffs hitting 60 countries are the twin shocks dragging stocks lower and keeping bonds under pressure today.
